_description: Gitea: a self-hosted Git service with a web UI, issues and pull requests. Alpine-based official image, everything under one data directory.
_comment: A RECIPE: `uxc deploy gitea` pulls the server, creates /srv/gitea with the right owner and registers the bind + a health check. The first start runs Gitea's own web installer, which writes /srv/gitea/data/gitea/conf/app.ini - so there is nothing to seed here, and no config file for a redeploy to argue with. Reach the installer at port 3000 (see _comment_ports below if the container is in an infra netns).

_source._comment_image: The official image, which is Alpine-based already - no third-party repack needed. Major-version tag: Gitea's minor releases migrate the database on first start, which is fine and automatic, but a major jump is a decision.

_comment_paths: The image runs as uid/gid 1000 (git). One directory holds everything: repositories, the database, avatars, LFS and the generated app.ini. That single path is the backup unit.
_comment_caps: The entrypoint fixes ownership under /data and drops to the git user via su-exec. Listed so the recipe also works with --caps minimal.

_registry._comment_volumes: EDIT THIS if /srv is not where your data lives. /data is everything Gitea keeps - back it up, together with a database dump if you move it off SQLite.
_registry._comment_env: USER_UID/USER_GID must match the owner of the data directory above. ROOT_URL is what Gitea writes into clone links and e-mails: set it to the address users actually reach, or every clone URL will point at the container. TZ affects issue timestamps.
_registry._comment_ports: In an infra netns the web UI is not reachable from the LAN. Publish it by adding ports, e.g. "ports": [ "3000:3000" ] (and "2222:22" for git-over-SSH), then set GITEA__server__ROOT_URL and GITEA__server__SSH_PORT to match. See docs/networking.md - a published port is a userspace proxy, so Gitea logs the forwarder as the client; use an fw4 redirect if that matters to you.
_registry._comment_health: Gitea's own endpoint, probed inside the container's network namespace - correct on the host stack and in an infra netns alike. start_period covers the first start, which initialises the database.
_registry.notes: Deployed from the 'gitea' recipe. Everything lives in /srv/gitea/data (owned by 1000): repositories, the SQLite database, LFS, and the app.ini that Gitea's installer writes on first start - that directory IS the backup. Finish the setup in the browser on port 3000; set the server's ROOT_URL to the address users reach, or clone links will point at the container. Git over SSH needs port 22 published or a reverse proxy; the web UI alone is fine behind Caddy. Gitea migrates its database automatically on a minor upgrade, so `uxc upgrade` is safe - but take a copy of /srv/gitea/data first anyway.
